svg.aria-label: How to write ળ — થ — અ — િ: 4 parts, ળ, થ, અ, િ, one after another
svg.title: Writing ળ — થ — અ — િ
svg.desc: 4 parts written one after another: ળ, થ, અ, િ (gujarati). The parts are in the order the hand writes them, which in Gujarati is the order they are typed: each sign comes after its consonant, even the i sign, which sits to the left of it. Each sign is drawn on its own, without the consonant it attaches to. Each part has its own group of frames; frame N of a group shows movements 1 to N of that part, the movement being added drawn in ink over the finished part, whose outline is read from _fonts/NotoSansGujarati-Static.ttf. Each part is drawn at its own scale from its own cited stroke order, so the strip does not show how large the parts are next to each other, how far apart they sit, or any join between them. Stroke order: ળ: t30apps.com, ‘Gujarati Alphabet Writing Practice’, version 1.0, ળ animation, first SVG path <https://www.t30apps.com/gujarati-alphabet-writing/>; થ: t30apps.com, ‘Gujarati Alphabet Writing Practice’, version 1.0, થ animation, first and second SVG paths <https://www.t30apps.com/gujarati-alphabet-writing/>; અ: t30apps.com, ‘Gujarati Alphabet Writing Practice’, version 1.0, અ animation, first and second SVG paths <https://www.t30apps.com/gujarati-alphabet-writing/>; િ: Tejas Gajjar, KanoAI, Gujarati barakhadi centre-line stroke templates (interpolate-svg/svgs/barakhadi), commit 9d3e294, 1_k/2_ki.svg, group g1 (stroke g1s0): the i sign drawn after the consonant (GitHub, 2026) <https://github.com/gajjartejas/KanoAI/tree/9d3e2949a3f265448e430e15329093ea3aa516b8/interpolate-svg/svgs/barakhadi>. Source notes on variation: ળ: The teaching app animates ળ as one continuous pen-down run in its first SVG path; its remaining path slots are empty. The run begins at the upper left, circles around the broad left bowl, rises through the narrow middle turn, crosses the high right arch, then descends the tall right spine into its lower foot without lifting. The app explicitly says that depicted forms and stroke orders can differ by source and should be treated as one variant, not a universal standard. The bundled Noto Sans Gujarati glyph preserves the broad bowl, narrow middle turn, high arch, tall spine, and lower foot, but its printed body is wider and more angular and its spine straighter than the animated school-hand form. This learner path preserves the source's left-bowl-to-middle-turn-to-right-spine order and zero-lift evidence while fitting the continuous run to the font's ink. Individual handwriting may narrow, round, simplify, retrace, or slant the bowl, turn, arch, spine, foot, and terminals differently. થ: The teaching app animates થ as two ordered pen-down runs. Its first SVG path begins at the right of the small upper loop, circles that loop, continues downward through the middle, sweeps left and around the broad lower body, then rises into the right shoulder. The animation lifts once and its second SVG path descends the separate tall right spine before turning through the lower-right foot. The remaining path slots are empty. The app explicitly says that depicted forms and stroke orders can differ by source and should be treated as one variant, not a universal standard. The bundled Noto Sans Gujarati glyph preserves the small upper loop, middle descent, broad lower body, right shoulder, tall spine, and lower foot, but its printed loop and body are wider and its spine straighter than the animated school-hand form. This learner path preserves the source's loop-and-body-before-right-spine order and one-lift evidence while fitting both runs to the font's ink. Individual handwriting may narrow, round, simplify, retrace, or slant the loop, body, shoulder, spine, foot, and terminals differently. અ: The teaching app animates અ as two ordered pen-down runs. Its first SVG path begins at the upper-left tip, sweeps clockwise around the open left curve, continues through the broad lower body, rises into the middle shoulder, and finishes through the small right arch. The animation then lifts once and its second SVG path descends the separate right stem before curving into the lower-right foot. The app explicitly says that depicted forms and stroke orders can differ by source and should be treated as one variant, not a universal standard. The bundled Noto Sans Gujarati glyph has the same open left curve, joined lower body, middle shoulder, small right arch, and separate full-height right stem, but its printed proportions are broader and its joins more angular than the animated school-hand form. This learner path preserves the source's body-before-right-stem order and one-lift evidence while fitting those movements to the font's ink. Individual handwriting may narrow, round, simplify, or slant either run differently. િ: In the template for કિ, and in all 34 consonant rows, િ is one pen-down run that starts at the right tip of the top hook, arcs up and to the left over the top, comes down the left stem and ends in a small foot to the right. HP Labs India's Lipi Toolkit Devanagari recognizer (native writers' pen traces of the matching Devanagari sign, written alone) agrees: its most common form of the i sign is two strokes (41 of 75 prototypes, 55%), but among its one-stroke prototypes (22 of 75) half start on the right and end at the lower left, as here. KanoAI's templates are hand-made centre lines, one path per pen-down run, which the app animates in the author's handwriting order and direction; one template per sign is placed beside every consonant, so the row counts show consistency, not separate writers. KanoAI's LICENSE file says MIT while its README says GNU GPL, so the licence is ambiguous: only facts are cited here (order, start, direction and pen lifts), and no template path data was copied. The path is fitted to the bundled Noto Sans Gujarati outline of the sign on its own. Handwriting varies by writer.
svg.text: How it is written — 4 parts, one after another
Part 3 of 4 — 2 strokes · 1 pen lift · 4 movements
Part 4 of 4 — one unbroken stroke · 3 movements
Part 1: stroke order after t30apps.com, ‘Gujarati Alphabet Writing Practice’, version 1.0, ળ animation, first SVG path
Part 2: stroke order after t30apps.com, ‘Gujarati Alphabet Writing Practice’, version 1.0, થ animation, first and second
Part 3: stroke order after t30apps.com, ‘Gujarati Alphabet Writing Practice’, version 1.0, અ animation, first and second
Part 4: stroke order after Tejas Gajjar, KanoAI, Gujarati barakhadi centre-line stroke templates
(interpolate-svg/svgs/barakhadi), commit 9d3e294, 1_k/2_ki.svg, group g1 (stroke g1s0): the i sign drawn after the
This order is attested, not standardised; the source records where it varies.
